title: Three Evenings and One Short Lantern
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）　|　核心词汇：joy　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 joy 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the singer ① brought the joy that no neighbour in the hall would have recorded, and he said the bringing was the whole of the evening. The ② joy, meaning the delight itself and not the lantern, ran three evenings and stayed unrecorded in the book; joy, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ kind of joy in that hall had the same short lantern beside it, and the ④ joy at the far door, meaning the song they kept for the children to sing and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Joy, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the singer said the recording is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the joy was the whole of the matter, meaning the blessing and not the delight. The ⑥ joy, meaning the blessing and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; joy, he said, is either something you bring or the only word that means both delight and a blessing. He said the blessing is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ joy had become a line in a note, and the note had become an argument about the short lantern. The ⑧ joy of the whole thing, the singer wrote in December, was one hall and three evenings of recording; joy, he said, is either the song at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ joy I remember is the joy recorded in the note, which closed in 1974 and is still recorded as the quietest in the hall. ⑩ Joy, my mother said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all joy, she said, is a blessing that has agreed to look like delight. She said the blessing was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 喜悦；欢乐（指礼堂里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 喜悦；欢乐（指那份欢喜本身，与灯笼相对）
C. 固定搭配：bring the joy 带来这份喜悦
D. n. 喜悦；欢乐（指留给孩子们唱的一支那一份）
E. n. 喜庆之事（抽象总称，指一处礼堂的喜悦之事）
F. n. 喜悦；欢乐（指便条里写到、被记下的的那一份）
G. n. 福气、欣慰（指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 欣慰（抽象总称，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: brought the joy that no neighbour in the hall would have recorded
The joy, meaning the delight itself and not the lantern

the joy at the far door

The joy of the whole thing

answers.why: bring the joy 意为“带来这份喜悦”，1967 年那位歌手把礼堂里没有一位邻居肯记录的一份喜悦做了一遍。
joy 意为“喜悦；欢乐”，指那份欢喜本身而不是灯笼，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记录。
joy 意为“喜悦；欢乐”，指礼堂里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一盏小小的灯笼。
joy 意为“喜悦；欢乐”，指最远那扇门口留给孩子们唱的一支那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
joy 意为“福气、欣慰”，指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份福气就是那件事的全部。
joy 意为“欣慰”，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份欢喜，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
joy 意为“喜悦；欢乐”，指便条里写到、被记下的的那一份，到 1972 年这一份成了便条里的一行。
joy 意为“喜庆之事”，歌手十二月写道，整件事的喜悦之事是一处礼堂和三个夜晚的记录。
joy 意为“喜悦；欢乐”，我记得的是便条里记录过的那一份，1974 年散去了，至今仍被说成礼堂里最安静的一份。
joy 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，喜悦是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的欢喜。
